ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Bax protein and Bak protein play specific roles in the apoptosis process of T lymphocytes. To explore the related mechanism, researchers used apoptosis-inducing reagents a and b respectively to treat T lymphocytes of different genotypes, and calculated the survival rate of the cells. The results are shown in the figure. Which of reagent a and reagent b has a better effect in inducing apoptosis of T lymphocytes?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Bax protein and Bak protein play specific roles in the apoptosis process of T lymphocytes. To explore the related mechanism, researchers used apoptosis-inducing reagents a and b respectively to treat T lymphocytes of different genotypes, and calculated the survival rate of the cells. The results are shown in the figure. Which of reagent a and reagent b has a better effect in inducing apoptosis of T lymphocytes?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The legend in the figure shows that the hollow bars represent reagent a, and the black solid bars represent reagent b; the vertical axis is “T lymphocyte survival rate (%)”. The horizontal axis is divided into four groups according to the presence or absence of the Bax and Bak genes: Bax+/Bak+, Bax+/Bak-, Bax-/Bak+, Bax-/Bak-. Judging from the bar heights, after treatment with reagent a, the T lymphocyte survival rate in each group is all about 30%; after treatment with reagent b, the survival rates are about 40%, 60%, 60%, and 80%, respectively, all higher than the corresponding reagent a. Then reason: The stronger the apoptosis-inducing effect, the more cell death there is, and the lower the cell survival rate after treatment. Since the cell survival rate of reagent a in each genotype group is lower than that of reagent b, this indicates that reagent a has a better effect in inducing T lymphocyte apoptosis.
